newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds shaky but off lows as long rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds shaky but off lows as long rates ease.

text.p: Greek bonds and FRNs managed to come off intraday lows but still looked shaky striving to find equilibrium amid easing long-term depo and implied rates from forex forwards, dealers said.
The drachma continued to gain ground against the ecu in quiet late dealing. Ecu/drachma breached the 310 level on the downside trading around 309.78/83.

"Fixed coupon bonds and floaters have cut their losses in late trade but there is still tension with offers and bids being hit in turns," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "Bonds are searching for equilibrium."
Tighter liquidity conditions linked to Thursday's announcement of an auction of FRNs on June 26 and the ensuing funding spiked interbank rates and hurt bonds, dealers said.
Bonds and FRNs received another blow from a heavier-than- expected schedule of auctions for the rest of 1997, bond dealers said.

"The central bank and the finance ministry should work together to ensure market stability," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "You cannot have the finance ministry seeking to raise money through auctions at the same time that the central bank drains liquidity."
The long-end of the forward and depo curves eased 10 to 15 basis points on forex-linked drachma inflows in late trade, dealers said.
The mark was quoted at 158.76/81 from Friday's 158.785 fix, the dollar at 275.63/73 drachmas from 275.560 and the ecu at 309.78/88 from 309.830 drachmas.
